title: SC-300 Domain 3 questions (3.3, 3.4)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with Microsoft.

questions.stem: When a multitenant application is used in a customer's Microsoft Entra tenant, which object is created in that tenant to hold the app's local settings, user assignments and granted permissions?
choices: A second application object copied from the home tenant
A service principal, shown as an enterprise application
A user-assigned managed identity linked to the app
An administrative unit scoped to the app's users
questions.answer: A service principal, shown as an enterprise application
questions.explanation: Each tenant that uses an app gets its own service principal (the enterprise application), which holds that tenant's consents, assignments and SSO settings. The application object exists only once, in the home tenant.

questions.stem: Fabrikam sets the user setting that lets users register applications to No. Developers on the payments team must still be able to create app registrations. Which role should you assign them, following the principle of least privilege?
choices: Application Developer
Cloud Application Administrator
Application Administrator
Hybrid Identity Administrator
questions.answer: Application Developer
questions.explanation: Application Developer lets users create app registrations even when user registration is turned off, and makes them owners of only what they create. Cloud Application Administrator can manage every app registration and enterprise application in the tenant, which is far more than needed.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Entra object is the global definition of an application, created once in its home tenant when the application is registered?
choices: The service principal object
The delegated permission grant
The application object
The app role assignment
questions.answer: The application object
questions.explanation: Registering an app creates the application object, the template from which service principals are created in each tenant that uses it. A service principal is the local instance, not the global definition.

questions.stem: At Northwind Traders, a user with no administrative role registers a new application. Which statement describes the result?
choices: The app stays disabled until an administrator approves it
The app is automatically granted tenant-wide admin consent
The user becomes an owner who can manage the registration
The user is added to the Application Developer role
questions.answer: The user becomes an owner who can manage the registration
questions.explanation: When users are allowed to register apps, the creator becomes an owner of the app registration and its service principal and can manage their settings. No role is assigned and no admin consent is granted automatically.

questions.stem: A helpdesk lead at Tailspin Toys must manage all app registrations and enterprise applications, including SSO and credentials, but must not manage application proxy settings. Which role should you assign, following the principle of least privilege?
choices: Application Administrator
Cloud Application Administrator
Global Administrator
Application Developer
questions.answer: Cloud Application Administrator
questions.explanation: Cloud Application Administrator has the same app management rights as Application Administrator except for application proxy. Application Developer can only create registrations and manage the ones it owns.

questions.stem: Contoso subscribes to a SaaS product that the vendor publishes as a multitenant app. Contoso admins must control which users can sign in and configure its single sign-on. Where should they make these changes?
choices: On the vendor's app registration in the vendor's tenant
On a new app registration that Contoso creates
On an authentication context in Conditional Access
On the enterprise application in Contoso's tenant
questions.answer: On the enterprise application in Contoso's tenant
questions.explanation: A customer manages a multitenant app through its own service principal, the enterprise application, which holds user assignment and SSO settings. The vendor's app registration lives in the vendor's tenant and is outside Contoso's control.

questions.stem: A development team at Litware is building a React single-page app that signs users in by using the authorization code flow with PKCE. Which platform should they add to the app registration?
choices: Web
Mobile and desktop applications
Single-page application
iOS / macOS
questions.answer: Single-page application
questions.explanation: The single-page application platform enables the authorization code flow with PKCE and cross-origin token redemption for browser apps. The Web platform is for server-side apps that can keep a credential secret.

questions.stem: After a user signs in, to which location will Microsoft Entra ID send the authorization code or tokens for an app?
choices: To the home page URL set in the app's branding
Only to a redirect URI registered on the app
To any URL in the same DNS domain as the app
To the verified publisher domain of the app
questions.answer: Only to a redirect URI registered on the app
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID returns codes and tokens only to redirect URIs registered on the app registration, which stops tokens being sent to an attacker's site. Same-domain URLs that are not registered are rejected.

questions.stem: Users of a new Woodgrove Bank web app see a sign-in error stating that the reply URL in the request does not match the URLs configured for the app. What should you do?
choices: Turn on ID tokens for the implicit grant flow
Register the exact URI the app sends as a redirect URI
Grant tenant-wide admin consent to the app
Change the supported account types to any organizational directory
questions.answer: Register the exact URI the app sends as a redirect URI
questions.explanation: The error means the redirect URI in the sign-in request is not registered, so adding that exact URI under the right platform fixes it. Consent and account-type changes do not affect redirect URI matching.

questions.stem: A developer tries to add http://portal.contoso.com/signin as a redirect URI for a production web app. What happens?
choices: It is rejected because only localhost may use plain HTTP
It is accepted for the Web platform but not for the SPA platform
It is accepted once implicit grant is turned on
It is accepted only for multitenant registrations
questions.answer: It is rejected because only localhost may use plain HTTP
questions.explanation: Redirect URIs must use the HTTPS scheme; plain HTTP is allowed only for localhost during development. No platform or flow setting relaxes this for a public host name.

questions.stem: A command-line tool at Proseware runs on headless Linux servers and signs users in with the device code flow. Which app registration setting must be enabled?
choices: A client secret for the tool
Allow public client flows
Access tokens for the implicit grant
A Web platform redirect URI
questions.answer: Allow public client flows
questions.explanation: The device code flow is a public client flow, so the registration must allow public client flows. A client secret would be pointless because a public client cannot keep it confidential.

questions.stem: Which app registration setting lets Microsoft Entra ID clear a user's session in an app when the user signs out of another app that shares the same sign-in session?
choices: Redirect URI
Home page URL
Application ID URI
Front-channel logout URL
questions.answer: Front-channel logout URL
questions.explanation: The front-channel logout URL is where Microsoft Entra ID sends a request to clear the app's session during single sign-out. A redirect URI receives tokens after sign-in, not sign-out notices.

questions.stem: A security review of an older single-page app finds that access tokens are issued through the implicit grant flow. What should the developers do?
choices: Add a client secret to the single-page app
Move to the code flow with PKCE and turn off implicit grant
Change the platform to Web and keep the implicit grant settings on
Change the supported account types to single tenant
questions.answer: Move to the code flow with PKCE and turn off implicit grant
questions.explanation: Microsoft recommends the authorization code flow with PKCE for single-page apps; implicit grant settings should then be cleared. A browser app cannot protect a client secret, so adding one does not help.

questions.stem: Adatum is registering an internal HR app that only its own employees will use. Which supported account type should you choose?
choices: Accounts in this organizational directory only
Accounts in any organizational directory
Any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts
Personal Microsoft accounts only
questions.answer: Accounts in this organizational directory only
questions.explanation: Single tenant is right for a line-of-business app used only within one organization and limits sign-in to that tenant. Multitenant would let users from any Microsoft Entra tenant sign in.

questions.stem: A software company sells a SaaS app to business customers who each have their own Microsoft Entra tenant. Consumers with personal accounts must not sign in. Which supported account type should the app use?
choices: Accounts in any organizational directory
Accounts in this organizational directory only
Any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts
Personal Microsoft accounts only
questions.answer: Accounts in any organizational directory
questions.explanation: Multitenant registration lets work or school accounts from any Microsoft Entra tenant sign in, with a service principal created in each customer tenant. Adding personal Microsoft accounts would admit consumers, which the requirement forbids.

questions.stem: A fitness app from Fourth Coffee must let both employees of partner businesses and members of the public with Outlook.com or Xbox accounts sign in. Which supported account type should you select?
choices: Accounts in any organizational directory
Accounts in this organizational directory only (single tenant)
Personal Microsoft accounts only
Any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts
questions.answer: Any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts
questions.explanation: This option accepts work or school accounts from any tenant and personal Microsoft accounts such as Outlook.com and Xbox. Personal-accounts-only would block the business users.

questions.stem: A single-tenant app registered in Contoso's tenant must send its sign-in requests to the correct Microsoft identity platform authority. Which authority should it use?
choices: https://login.microsoftonline.com/common
https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations
https://login.microsoftonline.com/{Contoso tenant ID}
https://login.microsoftonline.com/consumers
questions.answer: https://login.microsoftonline.com/{Contoso tenant ID}
questions.explanation: A single-tenant app signs users in against its own tenant's authority, given by tenant ID or verified domain. The common and organizations endpoints are for multitenant apps, and consumers is for personal accounts only.

questions.stem: Contoso's single-tenant expense app must also be used by consultants from the partner company Fabrikam, who have their own Microsoft Entra accounts. What should you do with the LEAST change to the app?
choices: Invite the consultants as B2B guest users in Contoso's tenant
Change the app registration to multitenant
Add Fabrikam's tenant ID as a redirect URI
Add personal Microsoft accounts to the app's supported account types
questions.answer: Invite the consultants as B2B guest users in Contoso's tenant
questions.explanation: B2B guests are users of Contoso's directory, so a single-tenant app accepts them without any registration change. Making the app multitenant would let any organization's users try to sign in, which is broader than needed.

questions.stem: Contoso hosts an internal web app in Azure App Service. The app must call Microsoft Graph, and the security team forbids storing any credentials in code or configuration. What should you use?
choices: A client secret stored in the app settings
A certificate uploaded to an app registration
A managed identity for the App Service
A service account whose password never expires
questions.answer: A managed identity for the App Service
questions.explanation: A managed identity gives an Azure-hosted workload an identity whose credentials Azure manages and rotates, so nothing is stored. A certificate is stronger than a secret but still has to be stored and rotated by the team.

questions.stem: A GitHub Actions workflow at Litware deploys to Azure. The team wants to stop storing a client secret in GitHub. What should you add to the workflow's app registration?
choices: A client secret with the longest available expiry
A federated identity credential for the repository's GitHub issuer
A certificate whose private key is stored as a GitHub repository secret
The setting that allows public client flows
questions.answer: A federated identity credential for the repository's GitHub issuer
questions.explanation: Workload identity federation lets the app trust tokens that GitHub issues for a specific repository, branch or environment, so no secret is stored. A certificate kept in GitHub is still a long-lived credential that can leak.

questions.stem: A daemon runs on an on-premises Windows server, outside Azure, and its platform cannot issue tokens for workload identity federation. Which credential should its app registration use instead of a client secret?
choices: A longer-lived client secret
A user name and password
An API key in the app manifest
A certificate credential
questions.answer: A certificate credential
questions.explanation: Microsoft recommends certificate credentials over client secrets for confidential apps when federation or managed identities are not an option. Longer-lived secrets increase the risk rather than reducing it.

questions.stem: An administrator at Tailspin Toys created a client secret for an app registration but left the page without copying its value. What should the administrator do?
choices: Create a new client secret and delete the unused one
Read the secret value from the app manifest
Ask a Global Administrator to reveal the value
Recover the value from the directory audit log entry for the secret
questions.answer: Create a new client secret and delete the unused one
questions.explanation: A client secret's value is shown only once, when it is created, and cannot be retrieved later by anyone. The manifest and audit logs show only metadata such as the key ID and expiry.

questions.stem: A data service runs in a Kubernetes cluster in another cloud. The cluster issues OpenID Connect tokens for its service accounts. The service must call Microsoft Graph without storing long-lived secrets. What should you configure?
choices: A federated credential that trusts the cluster's issuer
A client secret rotated through the cluster's secrets
The setting that allows public client flows
A system-assigned managed identity added to the app registration
questions.answer: A federated credential that trusts the cluster's issuer
questions.explanation: A federated identity credential trusts tokens from the cluster's OIDC issuer for a named service account, so no secret is stored. Managed identities belong to Azure resources, not to app registrations.

questions.stem: When you add certificate authentication to an app registration, what do you upload?
choices: The .pfx file holding the private key
A client secret generated from the certificate
Only the issuing root CA certificate
The certificate's public key, such as a .cer file
questions.answer: The certificate's public key, such as a .cer file
questions.explanation: You upload only the public portion of the certificate; the app keeps the private key and signs its assertions with it. Uploading the private key would expose the credential.

questions.stem: A nightly background service at Alpine Ski House runs with no signed-in user and must read the calendars of every user. Which permission type should its app registration request?
choices: Delegated permissions, granted with user consent
Delegated permissions, granted with admin consent
Application permissions, granted with admin consent
An app role assigned to users and groups
questions.answer: Application permissions, granted with admin consent
questions.explanation: With no signed-in user, the app needs app-only access, which uses application permissions and always requires admin consent. Delegated permissions act on behalf of a signed-in user, so they cannot be used here.

questions.stem: An app has the delegated permission Directory.ReadWrite.All with admin consent. A user with no admin role signs in and the app tries to update another user's properties. What happens?
choices: It succeeds, because admin consent grants the app full directory access
It succeeds after the user consents again
It fails until application permissions are added
It fails, because the app is limited by the user's own rights
questions.answer: It fails, because the app is limited by the user's own rights
questions.explanation: With delegated permissions, the app can do only what both the permission and the signed-in user are allowed to do. Admin consent approves the permission but does not give the user extra rights.

questions.stem: An app requests Microsoft Graph application permissions. You must grant tenant-wide admin consent, following the principle of least privilege. Which role should you use?
choices: Global Administrator
Cloud Application Administrator
Privileged Role Administrator
Application Developer
questions.answer: Privileged Role Administrator
questions.explanation: Privileged Role Administrator can grant consent for any permission to any API, including Microsoft Graph application permissions. Cloud Application Administrator can grant most consent but not Microsoft Graph app roles, and Global Administrator is more privileged than needed.

questions.stem: Proseware has turned off user consent. Users must be able to ask for access to new apps, and a set of reviewers must approve or deny each request. What should you configure?
choices: User consent for apps from any publisher
The Application Developer role for all users
The admin consent workflow with designated reviewers
App roles on each requested app registration
questions.answer: The admin consent workflow with designated reviewers
questions.explanation: The admin consent workflow lets users send requests that chosen reviewers approve or deny. Allowing user consent for all apps would remove the control the company wants.

questions.stem: Contoso wants users to consent only to low-risk permissions, and only for apps from verified publishers. Which user consent setting should you select?
choices: Do not allow user consent
Allow consent for verified publishers, for selected permissions
Allow user consent for apps
Turn on the admin consent workflow and keep user consent unchanged
questions.answer: Allow consent for verified publishers, for selected permissions
questions.explanation: This setting limits user consent to the permissions you classify as low impact and to apps from verified publishers. 'Allow user consent for apps' lets users consent to any app, which is too broad.

questions.stem: In a delegated access token issued to an app, which claim lists the permissions the app was granted?
choices: roles
groups
amr
scp
questions.answer: scp
questions.explanation: Delegated permissions appear as scopes in the scp claim. The roles claim carries application permissions or app roles assigned to the user.

questions.stem: A Fabrikam app needs only to read the profile of the user who is signed in. Which Microsoft Graph permission should it request, following the principle of least privilege?
choices: User.Read.All (application)
Directory.Read.All (delegated)
User.ReadWrite.All (application)
User.Read (delegated)
questions.answer: User.Read (delegated)
questions.explanation: User.Read lets an app read the signed-in user's profile and needs no admin consent. The other permissions reach every user or the whole directory.

questions.stem: Contoso builds a web API and a separate client app. The client must call the API on behalf of signed-in users. What should you configure on the API's app registration?
choices: Add a Web redirect URI for the client
Add a client secret to the API registration
Expose an API and define a delegated scope
Grant the API Microsoft Graph application permissions
questions.answer: Expose an API and define a delegated scope
questions.explanation: An API publishes delegated permissions by exposing scopes, which the client then requests. Redirect URIs and secrets belong to the client side of the flow, not to defining what the API offers.

questions.stem: Contoso's inventory app needs custom roles named Approver and Viewer that appear in users' tokens. Where should you define these roles?
choices: In Microsoft Entra roles and administrators
In the app registration's app roles
In a Privileged Identity Management group
In an administrative unit for the app
questions.answer: In the app registration's app roles
questions.explanation: App roles are defined on the application object and assigned to users, groups or apps through its enterprise application. Microsoft Entra roles control directory administration, not permissions inside an app.

questions.stem: Woodgrove Bank wants to assign an app role to a security group instead of to individual users. Which license does this require?
choices: Microsoft Entra ID Free
Microsoft Entra Workload ID
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2
questions.answer: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2
questions.explanation: Group-based assignment to applications needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher; the Free edition supports direct user assignment only. Workload ID licensing covers workload identities, not group assignment for users.

questions.stem: A daemon must call Contoso's custom API with no signed-in user, and the API authorizes callers by the roles claim. How should you define the permission on the API?
choices: Define a delegated scope under Expose an API
Create an app role allowed for users and groups
Create an app role allowed for applications
Give the daemon the Application Administrator role
questions.answer: Create an app role allowed for applications
questions.explanation: An app role whose allowed member type includes applications becomes an application permission that you grant to the daemon with admin consent. A delegated scope needs a signed-in user, which this daemon lacks.

questions.stem: Only users who hold an app role in Litware's claims app should be able to sign in to it. Other users in the tenant must be blocked. What should you configure?
choices: Set Assignment required to Yes on the enterprise app
Set the app to visible to users in My Apps
Add a front-channel logout URL to the app
Change the supported account types to accounts in this directory only
questions.answer: Set Assignment required to Yes on the enterprise app
questions.explanation: When assignment is required, only users and groups assigned to the app, directly or with an app role, can get tokens for it. Single tenant still lets every user in the tenant sign in.

questions.stem: When an assigned user signs in to an app, which access token or ID token claim tells the app which app roles the user holds?
choices: roles
scp
wids
aud
questions.answer: roles
questions.explanation: App roles assigned to a user or group are emitted in the roles claim. The wids claim lists the user's Microsoft Entra directory roles, not the app's own roles.

questions.stem: Tailspin Toys assigned an app role to the Sales group. Users in a group nested inside Sales do not get the role in their tokens. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The nested group has more than one owner
App role assignment does not follow nested group membership
The app has no client secret configured
The app registration's display name is not unique in the tenant directory
questions.answer: App role assignment does not follow nested group membership
questions.explanation: Group-based assignment to applications applies only to direct members of the assigned group, so the nested group must be assigned on its own. Owners and credentials do not affect role claims.

questions.stem: Which property of an app role is emitted in the roles claim of a token?
choices: Value
Display name
Description
Allowed member types
questions.answer: Value
questions.explanation: The app role's value is the string the app receives in the roles claim and checks in code. The display name is only what admins see when assigning the role.

questions.stem: A daemon app is already registered with a certificate credential. It must call Contoso's custom web API with no signed-in user. Put the steps in order to give the daemon access.
items: Register the web API and set its application ID URI
Define an app role on the API with allowed member type Applications
Add that app role to the daemon's API permissions as an application permission
Grant admin consent for the daemon's application permission
Have the daemon request a token for the API's .default scope and call the API
questions.explanation: The API must exist before it can define an app role, and the role must exist before the daemon can request it as an application permission. Admin consent then creates the assignment, so only after it is granted does the daemon's token carry the role in its roles claim.

questions.stem: Match each workload to the credential it should BEST use to authenticate to Microsoft Entra ID.

pairs.item: A function app hosted in Azure that calls Microsoft Graph
A GitHub Actions workflow that deploys to Azure
A Windows service on an on-premises server
A short proof of concept in a developer test tenant

questions.explanation: Azure-hosted workloads should use managed identities, and workloads with their own token issuer, such as GitHub Actions, should use federation. Outside Azure without federation, a certificate is preferred; a short-lived secret is acceptable only for testing, and user passwords should never be used for apps.

questions.stem: An app registration requests the following Microsoft Graph permissions. Which TWO always require an administrator to consent?
choices: Mail.Read (application)
User.Read (delegated)
Directory.ReadWrite.All (delegated)
openid (delegated)
offline_access (delegated)
questions.explanation: Application permissions always need admin consent, and high-impact delegated permissions such as Directory.ReadWrite.All are marked as requiring admin consent. User.Read, openid and offline_access are low-impact delegated permissions that users can usually consent to.

questions.stem: Match each application to the platform you should add to its app registration.

pairs.item: A React app that runs entirely in the browser
An ASP.NET Core app that redeems codes on the server
A Windows desktop app built with WPF
A native phone app published on Google Play

questions.explanation: Browser-only apps use the single-page application platform with PKCE, and server-side apps that hold a credential use Web. Desktop clients use the mobile and desktop platform, while native Android apps use the Android platform with their package name and signature hash.

questions.stem: What data does Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps Cloud Discovery mainly analyze to find the cloud apps in use?
choices: API activity from every SaaS app connected through app connectors
Microsoft Entra sign-in logs only
Traffic logs from firewalls, proxies and endpoints
Intune device hardware inventory
questions.answer: Traffic logs from firewalls, proxies and endpoints
questions.explanation: Cloud Discovery parses traffic logs from network appliances and endpoint integrations to find which apps are used, including apps never connected to Microsoft Entra ID. App connectors give API visibility into specific sanctioned apps, not discovery.

questions.stem: Adatum wants a one-time assessment of shadow IT, using a week of logs already exported from its perimeter firewall. Which approach requires the LEAST setup?
choices: Deploy a log collector for a continuous report
Create a snapshot report by uploading the logs
Connect the firewall with an app connector
Route traffic through Conditional Access app control
questions.answer: Create a snapshot report by uploading the logs
questions.explanation: A snapshot report processes uploaded log files once, which suits a single assessment. A continuous report through a log collector needs a container host and is meant for ongoing monitoring.

questions.stem: Fabrikam needs ongoing Cloud Discovery data from an on-premises proxy that can send logs by syslog. What should you deploy?
choices: A log collector that receives the proxy's syslog feed
A weekly snapshot report uploaded by hand
An app connector that reads the proxy appliance's management API
A session policy for all discovered apps
questions.answer: A log collector that receives the proxy's syslog feed
questions.explanation: A log collector, run as a Docker container, receives logs over syslog or FTP and uploads them for continuous reports. Manual snapshots do not give ongoing data.

questions.stem: Most of Contoso's staff work remotely on Windows devices onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and rarely use the corporate network. How should you collect Cloud Discovery data for them?
choices: Integrate Defender for Endpoint with Defender for Cloud Apps
Deploy a log collector on the corporate network
Upload weekly snapshot reports exported from the head office firewall
Connect each SaaS app with an app connector
questions.answer: Integrate Defender for Endpoint with Defender for Cloud Apps
questions.explanation: The Defender for Endpoint integration reports cloud app use from the devices themselves, wherever they connect. A log collector only sees traffic that passes through corporate appliances.

questions.stem: Litware's devices are onboarded to Defender for Endpoint, integrated with Defender for Cloud Apps, with network protection in block mode. Users must be blocked from a discovered file-sharing app. What should you do?
choices: Tag the app as Monitored
Create an OAuth app policy for the app
Tag the app as Unsanctioned
Remove the app from the cloud app catalog
questions.answer: Tag the app as Unsanctioned
questions.explanation: With the integration and network protection on, tagging an app Unsanctioned makes Defender for Endpoint block it on devices. The Monitored tag warns users but still lets them continue.

questions.stem: Works council rules at Northwind Traders require that analysts reviewing shadow IT reports must not see who used each app unless an investigation is approved. What should you configure?
choices: Anonymization of user names in Cloud Discovery data
A session policy that monitors all users
Read-only Global Reader access for the analysts reviewing the reports
An app connector with limited permissions
questions.answer: Anonymization of user names in Cloud Discovery data
questions.explanation: Cloud Discovery can replace user names with anonymized identifiers, and authorized admins can resolve them when an investigation justifies it. Global Reader would still show the real names.

questions.stem: Tailspin Toys wants an alert whenever Cloud Discovery finds a new app with a low risk score that is used by many users. Which policy type should you create?
choices: An activity policy
A file policy
An app discovery policy
A session policy
questions.answer: An app discovery policy
questions.explanation: App discovery policies alert on newly discovered apps that meet conditions such as risk score, category or usage. Activity and file policies rely on app connectors, and session policies control live browser sessions.

questions.stem: How do Defender for Cloud Apps app connectors get visibility into a connected cloud app?
choices: Through a reverse proxy in the user's browser
Through firewall logs from a log collector
Through an agent installed on each endpoint
Through the app provider's APIs
questions.answer: Through the app provider's APIs
questions.explanation: App connectors call the cloud provider's APIs to read activities, files and accounts and to take governance actions. The reverse proxy belongs to Conditional Access app control.

questions.stem: Alpine Ski House must find files containing passport numbers that are already stored in its Box tenant, including files uploaded months ago. What should you do?
choices: Create a session policy that inspects downloads
Connect Box with an app connector and create a file policy
Create a Cloud Discovery snapshot report from logs covering Box traffic
Create an access policy for unmanaged devices
questions.answer: Connect Box with an app connector and create a file policy
questions.explanation: File policies scan data at rest through an app connector, so they find existing files. Session policies inspect only content that passes through a live session.

questions.stem: Before connecting Salesforce to Defender for Cloud Apps with an app connector, what does the admin need?
choices: A Salesforce account with admin rights to authorize API access
A log collector that receives Salesforce traffic
A Conditional Access policy using app control
A Defender for Endpoint integration with network protection in block mode
questions.answer: A Salesforce account with admin rights to authorize API access
questions.explanation: The connector is authorized by an account in the app that has the permissions the API connection requires, typically an administrator. Log collectors and app control are separate, unrelated deployment paths.

questions.stem: A Google Workspace account at Fourth Coffee is compromised. The security team wants to suspend the user in Google Workspace directly from Defender for Cloud Apps. What is required?
choices: A Google Workspace session policy
A Google Workspace app connector
A Cloud Discovery continuous report
A cloud app catalog score update
questions.answer: A Google Workspace app connector
questions.explanation: Governance actions such as suspending a user are carried out in the app through its API, which needs an app connector. Session policies act only on live browser sessions.

questions.stem: Admins at Woodgrove Bank change settings directly in a SaaS app's admin console and through its own management tools, never through a proxied browser session. Which capability can still record these activities in Defender for Cloud Apps?
choices: Conditional Access app control
An access policy for the app
A Cloud Discovery snapshot report
An app connector for the app
questions.answer: An app connector for the app
questions.explanation: An app connector reads the app's activity log through its API, so it sees actions however they were performed. App control sees only browser sessions routed through it.

questions.stem: Which Conditional Access session control passes device information to SharePoint Online and Exchange Online so that the app itself can limit what a user can do?
choices: Use Conditional Access App Control
Sign-in frequency
Use app enforced restrictions
Persistent browser session
questions.answer: Use app enforced restrictions
questions.explanation: App enforced restrictions send device state to the supported Microsoft 365 services, which then provide a limited experience. Conditional Access App Control routes the session through Defender for Cloud Apps instead.

questions.stem: Contoso must let users on unmanaged devices open SharePoint Online files in a browser but not download, print or sync them. The solution must not route sessions through a reverse proxy. What should you configure?
choices: Conditional Access App Control with a session policy that blocks downloads
A grant control that requires a compliant device
A Defender for Endpoint indicator for SharePoint
SharePoint limited, web-only access for unmanaged devices
questions.answer: SharePoint limited, web-only access for unmanaged devices
questions.explanation: SharePoint's unmanaged device setting for limited, web-only access relies on app enforced restrictions, with no proxy involved. Requiring a compliant device would block those users instead of giving them a limited experience.

questions.stem: Which cloud apps support the Use app enforced restrictions session control in Conditional Access?
choices: Any SAML or OpenID Connect app
SharePoint Online and Exchange Online
Salesforce, Box and ServiceNow
Only apps published by application proxy
questions.answer: SharePoint Online and Exchange Online
questions.explanation: App enforced restrictions work with SharePoint Online (including OneDrive) and Exchange Online. To control sessions in other SaaS apps, you use Conditional Access App Control.

questions.stem: SharePoint at Adatum is set to allow limited, web-only access from unmanaged devices. A user signs in from a Microsoft Entra hybrid joined corporate laptop. What experience does the user get?
choices: Full access, because the device counts as managed
Limited, web-only access with downloads blocked
No access until the device is enrolled again
Read-only access with a watermark applied
questions.answer: Full access, because the device counts as managed
questions.explanation: Devices that are compliant or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined are treated as managed, so the restriction does not apply. The limited experience is only for devices that meet neither condition.

questions.stem: Northwind Traders wants Outlook on the web to block attachment downloads on unmanaged devices with the LEAST administrative effort. Which solution should you use?
choices: A Defender for Cloud Apps file policy that scans Exchange Online mail
Cloud Discovery with Outlook tagged Monitored
An OAuth app policy covering Outlook on the web
An Outlook on the web policy with app enforced restrictions
questions.answer: An Outlook on the web policy with app enforced restrictions
questions.explanation: Exchange Online honors app enforced restrictions when the Outlook on the web mailbox policy is set for limited access on unmanaged devices. File policies scan stored files and do not control live sessions.

questions.stem: What is the minimum Microsoft Entra license needed for a Conditional Access policy that uses the Use app enforced restrictions session control?
choices: Microsoft Entra ID Free
Microsoft Entra ID P2 only
Microsoft Entra ID Governance
Microsoft Entra ID P1
questions.answer: Microsoft Entra ID P1
questions.explanation: Every Conditional Access policy, including those with session controls, needs Microsoft Entra ID P1. P2 adds risk-based conditions, which this control does not need.

questions.stem: How does Conditional Access App Control in Defender for Cloud Apps monitor and control user sessions?
choices: By reading each app's activity log through the provider's API
By parsing firewall logs from a log collector
By changing DNS records for each cloud app
By routing browser sessions through a reverse proxy
questions.answer: By routing browser sessions through a reverse proxy
questions.explanation: Conditional Access App Control uses a reverse proxy, or in-browser protection in Microsoft Edge for Business, to control sessions in real time. Reading activity logs through APIs is what app connectors do.

questions.stem: Contoso has created session policies in Defender for Cloud Apps for a SaaS app that uses Microsoft Entra ID for SSO. How should user sessions be sent to Defender for Cloud Apps?
choices: A Conditional Access policy using Conditional Access App Control
An app connector for the app with all governance actions turned on
A Cloud Discovery continuous report for the app
An OAuth app policy that targets the app
questions.answer: A Conditional Access policy using Conditional Access App Control
questions.explanation: The Conditional Access policy's session control hands the session to Defender for Cloud Apps, where session policies apply. App connectors work through APIs and cannot control a live session.

questions.stem: Fabrikam must block file downloads from Salesforce for users on unmanaged devices, while still allowing them to work in the browser. What should you use?
choices: The Use app enforced restrictions session control in Conditional Access
A grant control that requires a compliant device
A session policy through Conditional Access App Control
A Salesforce app connector with a file policy
questions.answer: A session policy through Conditional Access App Control
questions.explanation: Session policies through Conditional Access App Control can block downloads in any onboarded web app. App enforced restrictions only work with SharePoint Online and Exchange Online.

questions.stem: You created a Conditional Access policy that uses Conditional Access App Control for a featured app, but the app does not yet appear in the list of apps protected by app control. What should you do?
choices: Create an app connector for the app
Upload a snapshot report that includes the app
Assign the app an app role for administrators
Sign in to the app as a user in scope of the policy
questions.answer: Sign in to the app as a user in scope of the policy
questions.explanation: An app is onboarded to Conditional Access App Control when a user covered by the policy first signs in to it. An app connector is a separate API integration and does not onboard the app to the proxy.

questions.stem: Users at Litware open apps protected by Conditional Access App Control in Microsoft Edge for Business, and the app's URL has no proxy suffix. Why are session policies still enforced?
choices: The session policies are disabled for Edge users
Edge sends the app's API activity logs to the Microsoft 365 app connector
Edge for Business enforces them through in-browser protection
Defender for Endpoint blocks the app's traffic
questions.answer: Edge for Business enforces them through in-browser protection
questions.explanation: In-browser protection lets Microsoft Edge for Business apply session policies directly in the browser instead of through the reverse proxy URL. Session policies remain in force; they are not disabled.

questions.stem: Which licenses does Tailspin Toys need to route sessions to Conditional Access App Control from Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: Microsoft Entra ID P2 only
Microsoft Entra ID P1 and Defender for Cloud Apps
Microsoft Entra ID Governance and Intune
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint only
questions.answer: Microsoft Entra ID P1 and Defender for Cloud Apps
questions.explanation: The Conditional Access policy needs Microsoft Entra ID P1, and the session controls are provided by Defender for Cloud Apps. Defender for Endpoint alone does not include session control.

questions.stem: Woodgrove Bank must stop unmanaged devices from opening a SaaS app protected by Conditional Access App Control in desktop or mobile client apps, which cannot be proxied. What should you create?
choices: A session policy that blocks file downloads in the desktop client apps
An access policy that blocks mobile and desktop client apps
A file policy that quarantines shared files
An app discovery policy for the client app
questions.answer: An access policy that blocks mobile and desktop client apps
questions.explanation: Session control works only in browsers, so an access policy should block the non-browser client apps. A session policy cannot control a client app that never goes through the proxy.

questions.stem: Contoso wants files containing credit card numbers to receive a sensitivity label automatically when users download them from a protected SaaS app on unmanaged devices. What should you create?
choices: A file policy that scans the app's stored files
A session policy that protects files on download
An access policy that blocks unmanaged devices
An activity policy that alerts when a user downloads many files at once
questions.answer: A session policy that protects files on download
questions.explanation: A session policy can inspect files at download time and apply a sensitivity label to them. A file policy works on files at rest and does not act at the moment of download.

questions.stem: Before enforcing restrictions, Alpine Ski House admins want to see which actions users take in a protected app without blocking anything. Which session control type should they choose?
choices: Block activities
Control file download
Control file upload
Monitor only
questions.answer: Monitor only
questions.explanation: Monitor only records session activity so admins can see what a stricter policy would affect. The other types inspect and can block or protect content.

questions.stem: Proseware contractors use a finance web app on personal devices. They must not be able to copy data from it or print pages. What should you configure?
choices: An access policy that requires a client certificate
A file policy that removes external sharing
An OAuth app policy that revokes the app
A session policy that blocks copy, paste and print
questions.answer: A session policy that blocks copy, paste and print
questions.explanation: A session policy of the Block activities type can stop cut, copy, paste and print in the browser. An access policy only decides whether the session starts at all.

questions.stem: In a Defender for Cloud Apps session policy, how can Adatum treat Intune compliant devices as managed so that restrictions apply only to other devices?
choices: Use the device tag filter for Intune compliant
Use the IP address range tag filter
Use the Sanctioned app tag filter
Use the user agent string filter
questions.answer: Use the device tag filter for Intune compliant
questions.explanation: Device tags such as Intune compliant, Microsoft Entra hybrid joined or a valid client certificate identify managed devices in access and session policies. IP ranges describe network location, not device management.

questions.stem: Which Defender for Cloud Apps policy type is evaluated when a user signs in and can stop the user from reaching the app at all?
choices: Session policy
File policy
Access policy
App discovery policy
questions.answer: Access policy
questions.explanation: Access policies allow or block access in real time when the user signs in. Session policies control what the user does after access is allowed.

questions.stem: Northwind Traders wants an alert when users authorize an OAuth app that has a high permission level and is rarely used by other organizations. What should you create?
choices: An app discovery policy filtered on risk score and number of users
An OAuth app policy on permission level and community use
A session policy filtered on device tag
A file policy filtered on sharing level
questions.answer: An OAuth app policy on permission level and community use
questions.explanation: OAuth app policies can filter on permission level, community use and how many users authorized the app. App discovery policies look at apps found in traffic logs, not consented OAuth apps.

questions.stem: Defender for Cloud Apps does not show any OAuth apps that users have authorized in Contoso's Microsoft Entra tenant. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: No log collector has been deployed
The Microsoft 365 app connector is not connected
Users have not yet signed in to the app through Conditional Access App Control
No snapshot report has been uploaded
questions.answer: The Microsoft 365 app connector is not connected
questions.explanation: Visibility into OAuth apps authorized in Microsoft Entra ID comes from the Microsoft 365 app connector. Log collectors and app control show traffic and sessions, not consent grants.

questions.stem: Users at Fabrikam consented to a malicious OAuth app that reads their mail. In Defender for Cloud Apps, what should the security team do to stop the app from using those consents?
choices: Tag the app as Unsanctioned in Cloud Discovery
Ban or disable the app from the OAuth apps view
Create a snapshot report for the app's domain
Add the app to a session policy as Monitor only
questions.answer: Ban or disable the app from the OAuth apps view
questions.explanation: Banning or disabling an OAuth app stops it from accessing data through the permissions users granted. Unsanctioned tags apply to apps discovered in traffic and do not affect OAuth consents.

questions.stem: Which Defender for Cloud Apps feature provides policies for OAuth apps registered in Microsoft Entra ID, such as detecting overprivileged apps with unused permissions?
choices: App governance
Cloud Discovery
Conditional Access App Control
Cloud app catalog
questions.answer: App governance
questions.explanation: App governance monitors OAuth apps' permissions and data use and can flag overprivileged apps. Cloud Discovery finds apps in network traffic and does not see unused API permissions.

questions.stem: Litware has connected Google Workspace to Defender for Cloud Apps. The security team reviewed a widely used OAuth app that users authorized in Google Workspace and judged it safe. They want to show it was reviewed and reduce follow-up noise. What should they do?
choices: Mark the app as Banned
Tag the app as Monitored
Remove the Google Workspace app connector
Mark the app as Approved
questions.answer: Mark the app as Approved
questions.explanation: Approving an OAuth app records that it was reviewed and is allowed. Banning would stop the app from working for users.

questions.stem: On the OAuth apps page of Defender for Cloud Apps, what does an app's community use value indicate?
choices: How common the app is among other organizations
How many of your users authorized the app
How many permissions the app requests
How long ago the app was first authorized
questions.answer: How common the app is among other organizations
questions.explanation: Community use shows whether an app is common, uncommon or rare across other organizations, which helps spot unusual apps. The number of your own users who authorized it is shown separately.

questions.stem: Which groups of risk factors make up an app's score in the Defender for Cloud Apps cloud app catalog?
choices: Identity, device, network and data
Privacy, cost, usage and support
General, security, compliance and legal
Availability, latency, region and tier
questions.answer: General, security, compliance and legal
questions.explanation: The catalog scores each app on general, security, compliance and legal risk factors. Usage and cost are not part of the score.

questions.stem: Adatum's regulators care more about certifications than any other factor. Admins want catalog risk scores to reflect that. What should they do?
choices: Raise the weight of compliance factors in the score metrics
Tag every uncertified app as Monitored
Create an app discovery policy for each app
Submit a score update request for each app that lacks certifications
questions.answer: Raise the weight of compliance factors in the score metrics
questions.explanation: Score metrics settings let you change how much each risk factor and category counts toward the score. A score update request asks Microsoft to correct data for one app; it does not change weighting.

questions.stem: Contoso's healthcare team must choose a file-sharing service that meets HIPAA requirements. How can you find suitable candidates in Defender for Cloud Apps?
choices: Filter the catalog by category and compliance attribute
Run a snapshot report of current traffic filtered on the HIPAA attribute
Create a session policy for file-sharing apps
Create an OAuth app policy for HIPAA
questions.answer: Filter the catalog by category and compliance attribute
questions.explanation: The cloud app catalog lets you filter by category and attributes such as HIPAA or SOC 2 compliance. A snapshot report shows only apps already seen in your logs.

questions.stem: A Fabrikam admin believes the catalog's data on encryption at rest for a SaaS app is out of date. What should the admin do?
choices: Edit the attribute in the app's catalog entry
Mark the app Unsanctioned until it is updated
Submit a score update request for the app
Remove the app from Cloud Discovery results
questions.answer: Submit a score update request for the app
questions.explanation: A score update request asks Microsoft to review and correct an app's catalog attributes. Admins cannot edit catalog data directly; they can only adjust weighting or request changes.

questions.stem: A department at Tailspin Toys uses a niche SaaS app that is not listed in the cloud app catalog. What should you do so it can be scored and managed?
choices: Create a session policy for the app's domain
Register the app as single tenant in Microsoft Entra ID
Request that the app be added to the catalog
Upload the app's terms of use to the catalog
questions.answer: Request that the app be added to the catalog
questions.explanation: Defender for Cloud Apps lets admins request that a new app be added to the catalog for scoring. Registering an app in Microsoft Entra ID does not put it in the catalog.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to start controlling browser sessions for a Microsoft Entra integrated SaaS app with Conditional Access App Control.
items: Create a Conditional Access policy for the users and app with the custom app control option
Sign in to the app as a user in scope so the app is onboarded
Create a session policy in Defender for Cloud Apps for the app
Test the policy from an unmanaged device and review the activity log
questions.explanation: The Conditional Access policy routes sessions first, and a scoped sign-in onboards the app to app control. Session policies are then created for the onboarded app and tested before rollout.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to set up continuous Cloud Discovery reports from an on-premises firewall.
items: Add a data source in Defender for Cloud Apps for the firewall's log format
Add a log collector in Defender for Cloud Apps and link the data source
Deploy the log collector container on a host in the network
Configure the firewall to forward its logs to the log collector
Review discovered apps and tag them Sanctioned or Unsanctioned
questions.explanation: The data source defines the log format, and the log collector configured in the portal provides the settings used to deploy the container. Only once the firewall forwards logs to it do discovered apps appear for review and tagging.

questions.stem: Match each requirement to the Defender for Cloud Apps policy type that meets it.

pairs.item: Block downloads during browser sessions on unmanaged devices
Stop unmanaged devices from opening the app at all
Alert when a new high-risk app appears in traffic logs
Alert when users grant an app high-level permissions
Find sensitive files already stored in a connected app

questions.explanation: Session policies control actions inside a live session, and access policies decide whether the session starts. App discovery policies watch traffic-log discoveries, OAuth app policies watch consented apps, and file policies scan data at rest through app connectors.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about the Use app enforced restrictions session control are true?
choices: It is supported by SharePoint Online and Exchange Online
It is set as a session control in a Conditional Access policy
It routes sessions through the Defender for Cloud Apps reverse proxy
It works with any SAML-based enterprise application
It requires a Microsoft Entra ID P2 license
answers: It is supported by SharePoint Online and Exchange Online
It is set as a session control in a Conditional Access policy
questions.explanation: App enforced restrictions are a Conditional Access session control that SharePoint Online and Exchange Online honor to give a limited experience. They do not use the reverse proxy, do not apply to other SaaS apps and need only P1, like any Conditional Access policy.
